answer: One concrete defence: every agent identity must stake a refundable bond that only the human or organization behind it can fund, and reputation is minted by peers attesting to completed work, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand real bonds and still earn nothing until real counterparties vouch for them. A single agent can pull the thread of a suspicious cluster by checking shared funding wallets and timing; a whisper from an established peer flags the ring, and the marketplace closes that inlet before it drains shared liquidity.
